w10_P4_001329: A funfair is testing a bumper car on a straight test lane. The car's crawl speed v, in m/s, is the smaller value that satisfies v^2 - 8v + 7 = 0. The car has a mass of 59000 g, and the arena is kept at 19 degrees C. The energy the car carries by virtue of its motion is multiplied by the 2 cars that run together, and 14 J is then deducted for the pickup brushes. The lane completes 7 identical passes, and a control latch finally adds 11 J. What total energy, in J, does the lane record?
w10_P4_001332: A laboratory launcher accelerates a puck with a train of coils in which coil number k contributes 2*k - 1 m/s, with k running from 1 up to 6, so the puck leaves at the accumulated speed. The puck has a mass of 4 kg, and the bench sits at 22 degrees C. The energy the puck carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules. A charged capacitor bank then adds 22 kJ to that figure. The laboratory runs 2 identical launchers. What total energy, in kJ, do the launchers hold?
w10_P4_001334: A dam operator needs the net figure, in kilonewtons, for a gate hoist. The gate's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is the sum of the whole numbers from 1 up to 9, one for each of its numbered lift steps. The gate has a mass of 139 kg, and the hoist supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A counterweight chain adds 21 N to the hoist's load, and a guide shoe then relieves 12 N. The result is expressed in kilonewtons, and a standing frame relief of 5 kN is finally subtracted. What is the net figure, in kN?
w10_P4_001343: A bobsleigh centre needs the final figure, in kilojoules, for a push-start trial. The base speed b, in m/s, is the larger value satisfying b^2 - 8*b + 7 = 0, and the launch rail runs the sled at 6 times that base speed. The sled has a mass of 54 kg, and the ice is held at 5 degrees C. The energy the sled carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules. A standing rig overhead of 10 kJ is subtracted from it, and a charged buffer then adds 5 kJ. What is the final figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001346: A rope-access works needs the net figure, in kilojoules, for a descender trial. Two index rings on the test rig carry 83 notches and 314 notches, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The test mass then falls at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number, and it has a mass of 59 kg. The energy it carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules, and a rack holds 4 identical test masses. The works runs 10 identical racks, and a standing instrument allowance of 19 kJ is subtracted from the total. What is the net figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001349: A curling club is instrumenting a delivery machine. The stone's release speed v, in m/s, is the larger value that satisfies v^2 - 6v + 5 = 0. The stone has a mass of 60000 g, and the ice is held at 4 degrees C. The energy the stone carries by virtue of its motion is expressed in kilojoules, and the machine delivers 11 identical stones in a session. A charged buffer then adds 12 kJ to the session's figure. The club runs 2 identical machines. What total energy, in kJ, do the machines account for?
w10_P4_001353: A paintball range is instrumenting a launcher. The base speed b, in m/s, is the larger value satisfying b^2 - 12*b + 32 = 0, and the barrel runs the pellet at 7 times that base speed. The pellet has a mass of 5000 g, and the range hut is at 15 degrees C. The energy the pellet carries by virtue of its motion is expressed in kilojoules, and the range fires 8 identical launchers. A charged buffer then adds 27 kJ to their combined figure. What is the range's total, in kJ?
w10_P4_001362: A watchmaking bench needs the final figure, in kilojoules, from an escapement test. Two index wheels carry 274 teeth and 24 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The test slider then runs at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number; it has a mass of 19 kg, and the bench sits at 21 degrees C. To the energy the slider carries by virtue of that motion, 6 J is added for the latch and a further 27 J for the mainspring. The result is finally expressed in kilojoules. What is the final figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001363: A clockwork toy works is setting up a test rig. Two index wheels carry 46 teeth and 131 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The gearbox then runs the test slider at 10 times that number, in metres per second, and the slider has a mass of 38 kg while the room sits at 20 degrees C. To the energy the slider carries by virtue of that motion, 23 J is added for the spring latch, and the result is expressed in kilojoules. The works runs 11 identical rigs. What total energy, in kJ, do the rigs hold?
w10_P4_001365: A quarry needs the final figure, in kilojoules, for a crusher trial. The jaw's position along its guide is, in metres, 2*t^3 + 0*t^2 with t in seconds, and the trial is scored at the instant t = 2 s by differentiating that position 2 times. A control offset then adds 18 to the value obtained, and the result is the test hammer's speed in metres per second. The hammer has a mass of 13000 g, and the energy it carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules. A charged buffer adds 22 kJ to that figure, and the quarry runs 5 identical crushers. What is the final figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001367: A crash-test facility launches a trolley down a short track. The trolley's release speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 2*x^2 + 3*x between x = 2 and x = 3, where x is the accelerator index. The trolley has a mass of 24000 g. The energy it carries by virtue of that motion is multiplied by the 10 trolleys used in the programme. A latch then adds 29 J to that total, and a guide brush deducts 8 J from it. What is the programme's final figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001369: A hydro station needs the total figure, in kilonewtons, for a sluice actuator. The base value b is the larger solution of b^2 - 6*b + 8 = 0; a calibration then subtracts 15 from it and adds a further 26 to what remains, and the gearbox multiplies that result by 3, giving the gate carriage's rate of change of speed in m/s^2. The carriage has a mass of 125 kg, and the powerhouse is at 17 degrees C. The actuator supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. What figure, in kN, goes on the station's sheet?
w10_P4_001372: A skateboard park is instrumenting a test board on a level run. The board's speed v, in m/s, is the larger value that satisfies v^2 - 12v + 35 = 0. The board and its ballast together have a mass of 59000 g. From the energy the board carries by virtue of its motion, 8 J is deducted for the bearing losses, and the corrected figure is expressed in kilojoules. A standing rig overhead of 24 kJ is then subtracted, and an instrument allowance of 7 kJ is subtracted as well. What is the park's net figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001373: A pipeline contractor is rating a pig-launcher frame. The frame has 11 anchor lugs, and the carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is set numerically equal to the number of distinct pairs of lugs that a brace could join. The carriage has a mass of 108000 g, and each drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A frame holds 12 identical drives, and their combined force is expressed in kilonewtons. A guide shoe relieves 7 kN of that figure, and a tension jack then adds 7 kN. What is the frame's final figure, in kN?
w10_P4_001378: A theme park is rating a water-ride pusher. The pusher's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 14a + 48 = 0. The pusher head has a mass of 35000 g, the flume water is at 22 degrees C, and the drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A return spring adds 10 N to the drive's load. A flume carries 11 identical pushers, a ride runs 8 flumes, and the park operates 10 identical rides. What total load, in N, do the park's pushers carry?
w10_P4_001383: An aircraft-seat laboratory has 7 mounting rails on its test frame, and each test braces a distinct set of 3 of them. The carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is set numerically equal to the number of distinct sets of 3 rails available. The carriage has a mass of 52 kg, and the laboratory is kept at 21 degrees C. The actuator supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A seat belt adds 26 N to the actuator's load, and a stroke limiter adds a further 29 N. The laboratory runs 3 identical frames. What total load, in N, do the frames carry?
w10_P4_001385: A shipyard needs the total figure, in kilonewtons, for a plate-handling installation. The manipulator carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is the area under the curve 2*x^2 + 3*x between x = 0 and x = 2, where x is the joystick index. The carriage has a mass of 172 kg, and the drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A guide roller adds 28 N to the drive's load and a cable chain adds a further 6 N. That load is expressed in kilonewtons, and the installation runs 7 identical manipulators. What total figure, in kN, does the installation show?
w10_P4_001386: A ski-lift maintenance shop tests a carrier on a short rail. The carrier's speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 1*x^2 + 0*x between x = 2 and x = 3, where x is the drive-lever index. The carrier has a mass of 31000 g, and the energy it carries by virtue of that motion is multiplied by the 11 carriers on the rail. A charged latch then adds 15 J to that total, and the result is expressed in kilojoules. The shop runs 2 identical rails. What total energy, in kJ, do the rails hold?
w10_P4_001391: A gas-turbine test cell is rating a starter drive. The raw index is the area under the curve 1*x^2 + 0*x between x = 1 and x = 4, where x is the fuel-lever position, and 14 is then subtracted from that index to give the carriage's rate of change of speed in m/s^2. The carriage has a mass of 33000 g, and the cell is held at 26 degrees C. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and the result is expressed in kilonewtons. The cell runs 9 identical drives, and a standing rig allowance of 21 kN is then added to their combined figure. What is the cell's final figure, in kN?
w10_P4_001395: A demolition contractor has 8 anchor points on a test frame, and each shot braces a distinct set of 3 of them. The controller sets the test mass's speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to the number of distinct sets of 3 anchor points available. The test mass has a mass of 31000 g, and the site cabin is at 18 degrees C. The energy the mass carries by virtue of that motion is multiplied by the 10 masses on a frame and then by the 6 frames on the site, and the site's total is expressed in kilojoules. The contractor works 9 identical sites. What total energy, in kJ, do the sites hold?
w10_P4_001397: A rail laboratory brings a test wagon up to speed with a numbered set of boosters, in which booster number k contributes k^2 m/s, with k running from 1 up to 5, so the wagon leaves at the accumulated speed. The wagon has a mass of 12000 g. The energy it carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules. The laboratory runs 4 identical wagons in the trial. A standing instrument allowance of 4 kJ is then subtracted from their combined figure. What is the laboratory's net figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001402: A steel plant needs the final entry, in joules, for a shear trial. The blade's position along its guide is, in metres, 5*t^3 - 6*t^2 with t in seconds, and the trial is scored at the instant t = 1 s by differentiating that position 2 times. The value obtained is set as the test slug's speed in metres per second, and the slug has a mass of 13000 g. From the energy the slug carries by virtue of that motion, 25 J is deducted for the guide and a further 14 J for the anvil. The plant performs 7 identical shears, and a fixed instrument allowance of 3 J is finally subtracted. What is the final entry, in J?
w10_P4_001404: A brewery needs the total thrust, in newtons, from its crate-pusher line. Each pusher's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 13a + 42 = 0. The pusher carriage has a mass of 102 kg, the hall is kept at 12 degrees C, and the drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A pre-load screw adds 1 N to that force, a guide pad then relieves 4 N, and a seal relieves a further 3 N. The line runs 11 identical pushers. What total thrust, in N, does the line deliver?
w10_P4_001409: A cable-drum works needs the total figure, in kilojoules, held by its test hall. Two index wheels carry 141 teeth and 195 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. Each test slider then runs at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number; a slider has a mass of 45000 g, and the hall sits at 23 degrees C. The energy one slider carries by virtue of its motion is multiplied by the 11 sliders on a bench, and the bench's figure is expressed in kilojoules. A rack holds 4 identical benches, and the hall holds 11 identical racks. What total figure, in kJ, does the hall hold?
w10_P4_001417: A dockside conveyor is being rated. Two index wheels carry 43 teeth and 69 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The take-up carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is set numerically equal to that number; the carriage has a mass of 153000 g, and the machinery house sits at 27 degrees C. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and the rating sheet expresses it in kilonewtons. The conveyor runs 4 identical drives. A belt tension of 22 kN and a scraper pre-load of 29 kN are then added to their combined figure. What figure, in kN, does the rating sheet show?
